Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{PS}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{QP}=b,$ and $\overset{\to }{PT}=c.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QT}$ in terms of $a,b,$ and $c.$
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,$ and $c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/2fafbd5822fd6edb578a2ada55a5787cc6f32b301911332115011b69cf0d664a.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=b,\,\overset{\to }{PT}=c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/be4803fec4af9e0009ea0d5a5683e17141a2086812a9df20bfdf976e849cc778.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT} \\  & =b+c\end{aligned}
$$
